before: Font resolvers loaded every face of each family that a document names.
after: Font resolvers load the faces that each client's laid-out text uses, and more faces when an edit needs them. A family that a user picks renders in its previous face on that client until its own face arrives.
reason: Font loading and the picked-family hold are local to each client. Shared nodes, text offsets, operations, and package serialization stay unchanged: a pick writes the picked family at once, and each client lays out with its own fonts as before.
